_meta.description: Severity definitions, score deductions, and remediation priority rules
_meta.author: Md. Sowad Al-Mughni <sowad.al.mughni@gmail.com>

CRITICAL.definition: Findings that expose user data, allow unauthorized access, or cause immediate security breach. Must be resolved before any user data can be trusted in production.
examples: API key or credential committed to source control
Row Level Security disabled on a table containing user data
Supabase service role key in client-side bundle
Authentication entirely absent on an endpoint that reads or writes user data
.env file tracked in git

HIGH.definition: Findings that significantly degrade reliability, scalability, or security posture. Will cause production failures under real load or expose exploitable attack surface.
examples: N+1 query pattern on a list endpoint
Database table created in migration but never queried (disconnected schema)
API routes with no authentication guard
Frontend pages calling endpoints that do not exist
Backend service not registered in application module
Auth checks implemented only in the UI layer

MEDIUM.definition: Findings that compound over time into HIGH or CRITICAL issues, or that cause degraded user experience at scale.
examples: Missing pagination on list endpoints
No file size limit on upload endpoints
Retry loop without maximum attempt cap
External API call inside a database transaction
Hardcoded mock data in a production code path
TODO/FIXME comments marking unfinished integrations
Missing indexes on foreign key columns

LOW.definition: Code quality and maintainability issues that slow future development but do not represent immediate risk.
examples: Missing HTTP cache headers on read-heavy endpoints
No dead letter queue on background workers
Unbounded storage without lifecycle policy
Duplicate query logic that should be extracted
Missing test coverage on critical paths

health_score.calculation: Start at 100. Deduct per finding according to score_deduction_per_finding. Floor at 0.

RED.meaning: Critical or systemic problems — not production-ready

auto_red_conditions: Disconnected schema (tables with zero application references)

remediation_sequence.rule: Always remediate in severity order. Never skip to a lower severity while CRITICAL findings remain open.

phases.action: Rotate secrets immediately. Enable RLS. Block launch.
Wire disconnected components. Add auth guards. Fix N+1 queries.
Add pagination, upload limits, retry caps. Remove hardcoded mocks.
Add caching, lifecycle policies, test coverage.

effort_estimates.CRITICAL_secret_rotation: 1-2 hours (key rotation) + git history rewrite if committed
effort_estimates.CRITICAL_rls_policy: 2-4 hours per table (policy design, implementation, testing)
effort_estimates.HIGH_n1_fix: 2-6 hours per endpoint (query rewrite, eager loading, testing)
effort_estimates.HIGH_schema_wiring: 4-12 hours per disconnected module (service, repository, integration)
